title: Grow a bloom
description: Change the lake conditions. Compare a floating bloom with a mat on the bottom.
projectQuestion: Which lake conditions would your idea need to notice, and which could it miss?
how: This is a teaching model, not a prediction for Lady Bird Lake. Its score describes conditions that support growth. It does not estimate toxins or tell you whether water is safe.

Temperature, nitrogen, phosphorus, light and flushing each change the score. The smaller nutrient support limits growth. These relationships and all curve settings are author-chosen examples, not fitted lake biology.
Mats receive less light at the bottom. We assume a shallow 0.5 m bottom and a fixed light-loss rate of 0.7 per metre. Real depth, shade and water clarity vary.
Monthly temperature examples come from selected shallow-water City visits. Some months have few samples or no samples. The nutrient and light presets remain invented teaching settings.
prompt: Before you try it: what evidence would you want to collect?

challenges.title: Follow the warmth
challenges.goal: At fixed other settings, compare a cool lake (≤15°C) with a warm lake (≥25°C).
challenges.hint: Use the same nutrients, light, flow and mode for both comparisons.

challenges.title: An October surprise
challenges.goal: Load the October temperature example. Keep its temperature and reach a growth score of at least 55.
challenges.hint: Change nutrients, light or flushing. A calendar month alone cannot rule out growth.

challenges.title: Change just one thing
challenges.goal: Start the supplied high-growth scene. Change exactly one control and lower the score by at least 20.
challenges.hint: Less light or more flushing can change this teaching score.

challenges.title: Look below the surface
challenges.goal: Compare a floating bloom and a bottom mat at the same settings.
challenges.hint: Use both growth modes. Notice the bottom-light assumption.

omissions: No toxin model, species competition, nutrient recycling, grazing, sediment chemistry or nitrogen fixation.
The flushing slider is a relative teaching control, not measured USGS discharge.
These monthly samples are not a complete seasonal climate record.
intro: Build a lake scene. Watch the growth conditions—not toxin risk.
caution: Illustrative, not field measurements. A high or low score says nothing about toxins.
monthlyNote: Real temperature examples, provisional: uneven City visits at three sites, shallow water only. Nutrients, sunlight and flushing in presets are simulated.
